title: Opt-level 2 miscompiles serial loop examples
description: sangoku run examples/hello.rs --opt-level 2 prints 'H' then halts returning 129 (0x81, the serial-control store value); primes/sort fail the same way; heap returns the correct 52. opt 0/1/z print correctly. At opt 2 rustc MIR-inlines write_volatile/read_volatile/str::bytes into write_str, so the LR35902 lowering of the inlined volatile store/load loop is wrong. Repro: cargo run -- clif examples/hello.rs - --opt-level 2, lower, run.
acceptance_criteria: hello/primes/sort produce correct serial output and return values at opt 2; a lowered/emulator regression covers the inlined volatile loop.
close_reason: Root cause: cg_clif lowered volatile_load/volatile_store as plain loads/stores; with MIR inlining Cranelift alias analysis forwarded the 0x81 store into the serial poll loop (infinite loop). Scalar volatile accesses now carry the Cranelift volatile MemFlag. hello/primes/sort correct at opt 2; regression tests/core_rom/volatile_poll.rs.

title: Enable MIR inlining for size opt levels
description: rustc enables MIR inlining by default only at opt-level 2/3, and Cranelift does not inline, so at s/z every trivial core wrapper (slice::Iter::new 305 B, Option::copied 191 B, read/write_volatile precondition_check 187 B, align_of, str::as_bytes) stays a call; s and z are byte-identical. Measured opt z -> opt 2: hello core 4264 -> 0 (ROM 6866 -> 2259), sort 18316 -> 7743, primes 22894 -> 9489, heap 63682 -> 32031. Pass -Zinline-mir=yes (and possibly -Zinline-mir-threshold tuning) for s/z, including the precompiled core/alloc builds. Blocked on the opt-2 miscompile.
acceptance_criteria: opt s/z ROM sizes at or below opt 2 for examples; examples pass at s/z.
close_reason: sangoku passes -Zinline-mir=yes at every opt level (hint threshold 50 at opt 0 so inlined bodies fit a 16 KiB bank). opt z: hello 6866->2265, primes 22894->9556, sort 18316->8777, heap 63682->32031. Numbers in wiki/concepts/size-baseline.md.

title: Model SM83 stack-slot access as an HL/F clobber instead of push/pop saves
description: Stack slot loads/stores are emitted as push hl; push af; ld hl,sp+N; ld r,[hl]; pop af; pop hl (7+ bytes) because the emitter cannot know whether HL/AF are live. Declare the HL (and F, since ld hl,sp+e sets flags) clobber to regalloc2 on spill/reload and stack-slot instructions so no save is needed. alloc.s at O0 has ~11.6k such wrapped accesses.
acceptance_criteria: Wrapped saves gone from stack-slot accesses where HL/F are not live; FileCheck fixture covers it; hello and heap ROM sizes recorded before/after.
notes:
Step 1 done (wasmtime c4b3e3ca): spills no longer save AF; flags never live across insts. Load/store B/C/D/E/A = push hl; ld hl,sp+N+2; ld r,[hl]|ld [hl],r; pop hl. H/L keep an A-based path. check-spills passes (12096 access, 1024 pressure, Rust probes). Sizes opt0 before->after: primes 30874->26265, sort 23869->20474, hello 8768->7714, heap 93311->77754; opt s: 28284->24016, 22550->19309, 8131->7196, 80365->66583. Remaining: drop push/pop hl when HL is dead, which needs post-regalloc physical-reg liveness (spill edits bypass operand constraints).
Step 2 complete in wasmtime c5535f19: emission uses physical-register liveness after regalloc, including spill/reload edits and CFG successors. LoadStack8/StoreStack8 omit HL saves when dead and preserve live A for H/L stores. Binary emission and RGBDS printing agree. Added loop/dataflow and scratch-liveness tests plus lower/stack-liveness.clif. Gates: 36 SM83 backend tests and 1 dataflow test pass; spill audit passes 12096 access, 1344 liveness, 1024 pressure cases and Rust probes; all 171 project nextest tests pass. Rebuilt pinned cg_clif backend. Linker-map used bytes before -> after: hello O0 3616 -> 3324, z 2265 -> 2089; heap O0 55382 -> 48102, z 32031 -> 26191. Heap O0 still exceeds 32768; optimized heap ROM executes and returns 52. Clippy, fmt, LSP diagnostics and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Dead HL saves removed using post-regalloc liveness, live scratch values preserved; FileCheck and emulator coverage pass, ROM sizes recorded.

title: Fix LR35902 indirect-call clobbers and trampoline return address
description: The CallIndirect operand collector re-adds D/E clobbers after gen_call_info already excluded return registers, creating a clobber/definition conflict when an i32 result uses D. Both direct and indirect collectors also incorrectly remove argument registers and the indirect target registers from the clobber set, potentially keeping live arguments or a reused function pointer in registers overwritten by the callee. Forward the clobber set computed by gen_call_info unchanged, matching other Cranelift backends. Validate two consecutive indirect split-i64 calls sharing the target and a live argument.
acceptance_criteria: Direct and indirect split-i64 calls with register/stack arguments and return-area results execute correctly; a reused function pointer and argument remain valid across consecutive indirect calls; no clobber/definition conflict or regalloc panic.
notes: Implementation forwards gen_call_info clobbers unchanged for direct and indirect calls. The RGBDS pretty-printer previously emitted an undefined call_indirect pseudo-instruction, and the binary trampoline adjusted its return PC by the wrong amount. Both now use the same fixed-length 12-byte trampoline preserving AF and HL while using caller-saved DE; return PC adjustment matches its actual length. Consecutive indirect split-i64 calls test target/argument liveness.

title: Legalize LR35902 i64 values into two i32 halves before machine lowering

CLIF integers are signless, so this covers Rust u64 and i64 with operation-specific signedness. Preserve little-endian memory layout and propagate the pair through block parameters, branches, calls, and returns. Start with constants, bitwise ops, add/sub carry chains, signed/unsigned comparisons, select, load/store, integer extensions and truncation, isplit/iconcat, shifts and rotates; explicitly diagnose remaining unsupported i64 opcodes rather than silently truncate. Integrate in the Cranelift compile pipeline so both sangoku lower and cg_clif use the same transformation. Keep i128 and floating-point legalization in separate follow-ups.

Added narrower shift expansion to existing i16 machinery, carry/borrow arithmetic, multiplication, comparisons, selects, counts/reordering, conversions and native/big-endian memory splitting. Optimizer-generated bmask and wide select conditions now lower correctly. Direct and repeated indirect split-i64 calls execute correctly after fixing trampoline/clobbers in sangoku-57q.3.1. Common Debug escaping also reaches White_Space, Grapheme_Extend, Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, Cf, and Cn_Planes_0_3 through private char helpers. Thus several tables are indirectly needed by core formatting and alloc behavior; do not cfg stable APIs or make them panic merely to drop tables. Next step is measuring per-table reachability in linked ROM; consider dropping only optional/unstable APIs or using a documented target profile if exact upstream semantics are intentionally relaxed.

# SM83 shifts and rotates audit

`sangoku-mt4.4` recommends constant specialization and optimization-dependent
variable helpers. This audit changes no production lowering or runtime code.
Implementation follows in `sangoku-9tk` (constants) and `sangoku-clp` (variables).

Run the bounded comparison with:

```bash
cargo run --example audit-shifts -- --artifacts build/shift-audit-fast \
  --output build/shift-audit-fast/results.json
```

Defaults cover counts 0, 1, 8 and width-1, four explicit values and two seeded
random words, body/caller modes and the shortlisted candidates. More than eight
random samples requires `--full`; exhaustive checks require both `--full` and
`--exhaustive16`. Ordinary `cargo test` uses small representative matrices.

## Decisions

| Operation | 16-bit constant | 32-bit constant | Variable, both widths |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Left shift | Replace: YES | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |
| Logical right shift | Replace: YES | Replace: YES | Adopt: YES |
| Arithmetic right shift | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |
| Rotate left | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |
| Rotate right | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES; currently absent | Adopt: YES |

For constants, select byte moves plus residual bit operations (`lanes`). For
16-bit left shifts by 2–7, prefer the `pair` candidate using `ADD HL,HL`.
Zero-count identity: Replace: NO. Keep the identity operation.

For variable counts, select `loop` for unoptimized/size intent and `byte-loop`
for speed intent. The byte loop adds 28 clocks for counts below eight; a known
small count range can favor the compact loop even in speed builds. Mask CLIF
counts by width-1. Rust checked shifts need their full-width range guard before
count truncation; masked counts alone do not implement checked shifts.

Blanket outlining: Replace: NO. Inline tiny constant sequences. For helper
bytes H, per-use call bytes C and inline bytes I, outline for strict ROM savings
only when I>C and uses exceed H/(I-C). The CSV records the first saving use
count, including argument packing and live-value preservation. CALL/RET alone
adds 40 T-cycles.

## Measured costs

These body figures include RET in CPU T-cycles. Bytes are linked instruction
bytes. Candidates use the audit ABI; their costs are targets for implementation,
not guarantees about future allocated compiler output.

| Constant case | Current bytes / clocks | Selected bytes / clocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16-bit left by 1 | 7 / 40 | 6 / 36 |
| 16-bit left by 7 | 31 / 136 | 12 / 88 (`pair`) |
| 16-bit left by 8 | 35 / 152 | 2 / 20 |
| 16-bit right by 8 | 35 / 152 | 4 / 28 |
| 16-bit right by 15 | 63 / 264 | 7 / 40 |
| 32-bit right by 1 | 25 / 168 | 16 / 84 |
| 32-bit right by 8 | 81 / 392 | 10 / 60 |
| 32-bit right by 31 | 265 / 1128 | 14 / 76 |

Variable means below give equal weight to every legal normalized count, from
the retained full run. They are not averages over the sparse default cases.

| Width / operation | Bit loop bytes / mean clocks | Byte loop bytes / mean clocks | Byte loop min–max clocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 / logical shifts | 16 / 284.5 | 30 / 213 | 80–352 |
| 16 / arithmetic right | 16 / 284.5 | 32 / 217 | 80–360 |
| 16 / rotations | 18 / 344.5 | 32 / 241 | 80–408 |
| 32 / logical shifts | 28 / 836.25 | 44 / 385 | 128–648 |
| 32 / arithmetic right | 28 / 836.25 | 46 / 397 | 128–672 |
| 32 / rotations | 30 / 960.25 | 46 / 413 | 128–704 |

Manual helper body stack is 2 bytes for 16-bit and 4 for 32-bit, including the
return address and incoming arguments. Table ROM and owned scratch RAM are
zero. Complete caller, live-input caller, inline and inline-live measurements,
stack peaks and sharing thresholds are in [shifts.csv](shifts.csv). JSON adds
observed register changes; callers must treat AF/BC/DE/HL as clobbered unless
the final compiler ABI establishes narrower preservation.

The 16-bit input is B/C, output A/B, variable count A. The 32-bit input is
B/C/A/[entry SP+2], output A/B/C/D, variable count [entry SP+3]. SDCC uses a
bridge to its native ABI: 52 clocks for 16-bit, 84 for constant 32-bit and 132
for variable 32-bit. CSV native costs subtract that fixed bridge; compare
complete bridged callers for this backend rather than claiming native SDCC
is uniformly slower.

## Evidence and reproduction

Fixtures and compiler probes live in `tests/fixtures/shifts`; the executable
comparison is `tests/support/src/shifts.rs`. SDCC speed/size snapshots come from
the clean `/home/takashi/sdcc` revision 17147. Exact commands, source hash and
tool versions are in `tests/fixtures/shifts/provenance.json`. Optional `--sdcc
PATH` regenerates both profiles and checks normalized instruction parity.

The historical full report is `build/shift-audit/results.json`; retained
assembly/ROMs and compiler output are alongside it. Its CSV is committed here.
That run passed 2,204,465 candidate cases, 5,242,880 exhaustive constant-16
cases and 47,424 compiler executions. Reproduction, explicitly opt-in:

```bash
cargo run --example audit-shifts -- --full --samples 128 --seed 0 \
  --exhaustive16 --output build/shift-audit/results.json \
  --csv wiki/audits/shifts.csv
```

The final bounded run passed 1,968 candidate and 252 compiler executions,
plus 72 actual Rust shift/guard probes, with zero errors. Coverage includes
sign bits, byte boundaries, width-1, oversized masked counts, live inputs,
restored SP, return frames and stack-only writes. Rust guarded payload/validity
probes include count 65536; full core Option-return ABI remains untested.

Supported native CLIF outputs are assembled and byte-compared to emitted
machine code. Missing compiler operations use the explicit `bits` reference.
SRA flags/timing and auto-indexed HL loads/stores have independent emulator
regressions. The emulator models flat-memory instruction timing, without
interrupts, peripherals or banking. See the [testing log](../log/2026-11-06-16-40.md).
